newsitem.title: USA: Interlake to explore material handling sale.
newsitem.headline: Interlake to explore material handling sale.

text.p: Interlake Corp said Tuesday it will explore the sale of all of its material handling businesses to allow the company to pay down debt and concentrate on its two engineered materials businesses.

In fiscal 1996, material handling had operating profit of $24.8 million on net sales of $452.1 million. Interlake as a whole reported operating profit from continuing operations of $63.7 million on net sales from continuing operations of $709.6 million.

Interlake's material handling segment designs, manufactures and sells storage rack, shelving, conveyors and related equipment for use in warehouses, distribution centers and retail stores. It also supplies equipment for retail display and office interiors.
The U.S. material handling operations are conducted at manufacturing plants in Pontiac, Ill.; Sumter, S.C.; Lodi, Calif., and Shepherdsville, Ky.
Besides its United States presence, the business has a significant market share in the United Kingdom, Belgium, Australia and Germany, Interlake said.
"Material Handling is a good business,"said chairman W. Robert Reum, adding the copany would only sell it "if we can receive a price which meets our strategic objectives."

Reum said Interlake would focus on its special materials and aerospace components businesses. Hoeganaes Corp, through which Interlake conducts its special materials business, produces ferrous metal powders. Its aerospace components operation, conducted through Chem-tronics Inc, produces lightweight, fabricated products for commercial and military aerospace applications.
